Structuration theory is a sociological theory that provides an integrated account of the relationship between structure and action, and the relationship between structure, action, and agency.

structuration theory is a theory of the production of social life through time and space, which is based on the notion that human action is mediated through the reproduction of the social structures of society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
structuration theory provides a framework for understanding social practices and the way in which social systems are produced and reproduced through human agency.
the theory provides a way of understanding the relationship between the social and the technical, and the way in which this relationship is constantly being reconstituted.

structuration theory provides a framework for the analysis of how social systems are reproduced, changed, or transformed through the interaction of human agency and the social structure of which they are part.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the world is not becoming a homogeneous arena of global business and global attitudes, but is becoming a more complex and heterogeneous place.
there is no one way of doing things, and that there are multiple ways of doing things.
the use of technology is not simply an instrumental process of applying tools to solve problems.
